contentBlocks.text: This week you wrote a topic sentence, supporting details, and a closing sentence. Today: combine them into one complete paragraph!

A complete paragraph puts all three pieces in order: topic sentence first, then 2-3 supporting details, then a closing sentence — all written together as one connected piece, not three separate lists. Copy your topic sentence, your two supporting details, and your closing sentence from this week onto one page, in that order, as a single paragraph.
You just wrote a complete paragraph, start to finish! Tomorrow we'll review the whole week and share your finished paragraph.

objectives: Assemble a topic sentence, supporting details, and a closing sentence into one connected paragraph
Recognize that a paragraph is a single connected piece of writing, not a list of separate sentences
materialsNeeded: All three of this week's earlier worksheets
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Gather all three of this week's pieces (topic sentence, 2 supporting details, closing sentence).
2. Explain that today's job is combining them in order, as one paragraph.
3. Have the child copy all four sentences onto the worksheet in order.
4. Read the finished paragraph aloud together, checking it flows.
5. Preview tomorrow's celebration/review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: number each sentence 1-4 in the order they'll appear before copying, as a scaffold
Ready for more: ask the child to add one transition word (like 'Also' or 'Finally') between two of the sentences
This is the payoff moment for the whole week — celebrate the finished paragraph as real, complete writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an assembly activity — check that all four sentences (topic, 2 details, closing) appear in the correct order and connect logically as one paragraph.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 2 Writing standard W.2.1/W.2.2 in full (a complete piece with topic, supporting reasons/facts, and a concluding statement), synthesizing the whole week's work.

generationData.instructions: Copy your complete paragraph: topic sentence, then supporting details, then closing sentence.
